paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption_used: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring shows that nearly half of all samples (49.0%) exhibit zero ambiguity standard deviation (Std: 0.0), followed by Std: 0.47 at 38.0%, with the remaining samples distributed between Std: 0.82 at 7.0% and Std: 0.94 at 5.0%. In the inner ring, Max Ambiguity of 1 accounts for approximately 39.0% of samples, Max: 2 represents the largest inner-ring segment at 47.7%, and Max: 3 comprises 14.2%. The two rings together indicate that the majority of samples exhibit low ambiguity across both measures.
model_annotation: The chart displays the distribution of samples across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity. The donut chart consists of two concentric rings, with the outer ring showing four slices representing ambiguity standard deviation and the inner ring showing three slices for maximum ambiguity. The outer ring's slices are labeled as follows: Std: 0.0 in dark blue at 49.0%, Std: 0.47 in blue at 38.0%, Std: 0.82 in light blue at 7.0%, and Std: 0.94 in light blue at 5.0%. The inner ring's slices are: Max: 1 in blue at 39.0%, Max: 2 in light blue at 47.7%, and Max: 3 in dark blue at 14.2%. Both rings have percentage labels inside their respective slices. A legend is provided to the right of the chart, detailing the color coding for each ambiguity level. The segments in each ring appear to be arranged in descending order of size.
